newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh survey detects gold, silver.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh survey detects gold, silver.

text.p: Bangladeshi scientists have discovered gold and silver in sub-soil rocks in the country's northern region, officials said on Tuesday.

"We have detected ores of gold, silver and zinc during recent geological surveys in at least two northern districts," Muhammad Khurshid Alam, Director General of the state-run Geological Survey of Bangladesh (GSB), told Reuters on Tuesday.
He said Bangladesh, however, needed to conduct a "massive evaluation" to determine if the deposits are economically viable for mining.
"If we believe in our wisdom and equipment, we have detected gold and silver. But the question is whether those are minable or not. That needs extensive research," he said.
Alam said the GSB scientists had discovered between 1.3 and 2.0 parts per million (ppm) of gold ore in drilled rocks in the districts of Naogaon and Dinajpur.
"The percentage looks encouraging if compared with other countries which are mining gold," he said.
The GSB chief said his scientists had also discovered a silver deposit of up to 100 grams per tonne of rock in the Dighipara area of Dinajpur district.
"This too appears prospective from an international comparison...," he said.
Alam said the recent detection of arsenic contents in sub-soil water in various parts of Bangladesh could indicate the presence of gold and silver.
"Arsenic is an indicative element. It (arsenic) has a relation with gold and silver".
He said he had told top government leaders, including Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, about the discovery. "We are preparing for further investigation and survey," he said.
